title: The Seesaw: wider stop, smaller size
hook: Always buy 100 shares? Nice round number.
takeaway: Fix the risk first (say 1% of the account), then let the stop set the size: shares = risk ÷ stop distance, rounded down. A wider stop means fewer shares and the same dollars at risk. Buying the same share count every time lets your stop decide your risk instead.
emotion: 'oh no, that's me': the habit of a round share count, then relief as the beam levels
new_angle: Lore 003 defined 1R; this entry keeps 1R the same dollar amount when the stop moves, by changing the share count.
